title: Nvidia discussing $2,000-per-GPU annual fee for software that runs agents on AI factories
gist: A SemiWiki forum post relays that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, at GTC Berlin on October 22, put Nvidia's agent-software licensing at roughly $2,000 per GPU per year. A FourWeekMBA scenario of five million paid licenses implies $10 billion a year, or $50 billion over five years, though Nvidia has not disclosed coverage or scope.

insights.claim: Jensen Huang said Nvidia's licensing for software that runs agents on AI factories is about $2,000 per GPU per year, and that software licensing will become increasingly a major part of the company's business.
insights.speaker: Jensen Huang
insights.so_what: Signals Nvidia's shift toward recurring software revenue layered on hardware.
insights.quote: Software licensing will become increasingly a major part of our company’s business.
insights.locator: Huang discussed the pricing at GTC Berlin

insights.claim: At $2,000 per GPU per year, five million licensed GPUs would yield $10 billion annually and $50 billion over five years, assuming customers keep renewing.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: A illustrative scenario, not a disclosed Nvidia target.

insights.claim: Nvidia has not disclosed how many GPUs the fee would cover, whether $2,000 is the standard price, which software it includes, or whether products overlap.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: The revenue figure cannot be underwritten until pricing and scope are clarified.

insights.claim: Ben Pouladian bets that OpenShell becomes the standard security layer for enterprise AI, since enterprises deploying agents need security, governance and someone accountable for keeping the stack running.
insights.speaker: Ben Pouladian
insights.so_what: Agent security and governance could be a monetizable software moat for Nvidia.

insights.claim: GTC Berlin framed Nvidia's push as an AI infrastructure business spanning chips, software and AI-agent security.
insights.speaker: B
